<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/service-messaging`, `@objectstack/service-push`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-push/src/push-service.ts`, `packages/spec/src/system/push-server-origin.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/push-service.mdx`  _(via RegisterDeviceRequestSchema (symbol, a top-level const), sys_user_device (symbol, a field of const object arObjects; a field of const object deObjects; a field of const object enObjects; a field of const object esESObjects; a field of const object frObjects; a field of const object jaJPObjects; a field of const object koObjects; a field of const object ptBRObjects; a field of const object ruObjects; a field of const object zhCNObjects; a field of const object zhHantObjects))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via sys_user_device (symbol, a field of const object arObjects; a field of const object deObjects; a field of const object enObjects; a field of const object esESObjects; a field of const object frObjects; a field of const object jaJPObjects; a field of const object koObjects; a field of const object ptBRObjects; a field of const object ruObjects; a field of const object zhCNObjects; a field of const object zhHantObjects))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via UserDevice (symbol, a top-level const object), sys_user_device (symbol, a field of const object arObjects; a field of const object deObjects; a field of const object enObjects; a field of const object esESObjects; a field of const object frObjects; a field of const object jaJPObjects; a field of const object koObjects; a field of const object ptBRObjects; a field of const object ruObjects; a field of const object zhCNObjects; a field of const object zhHantObjects))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-push/src/push-service.ts`, `packages/spec/src/system/push-server-origin.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **221** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4564d6fa5b79764676d554de1cedd5946ca0f120` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1a3c380470eb00a7f12d78da4ea29fe3b43b212e` — the merge of head `6dc84f5e922e380bc96cf43431a4c3ab950e60e4` into base `4564d6fa5b79764676d554de1cedd5946ca0f120`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1a3c380470eb00a7f12d78da4ea29fe3b43b212e && git checkout 1a3c380470eb00a7f12d78da4ea29fe3b43b212e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4564d6fa5b79764676d554de1cedd5946ca0f120 6dc84f5e922e380bc96cf43431a4c3ab950e60e4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4564d6fa5b79764676d554de1cedd5946ca0f120 && git merge --no-ff 6dc84f5e922e380bc96cf43431a4c3ab950e60e4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4564d6fa5b79764676d554de1cedd5946ca0f120
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4564d6fa5b79764676d554de1cedd5946ca0f120` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `48036dd19332b8cf1856fd162bb61996411d738f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/system/push-device.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/system/push-server-origin.ts` + `packages/spec/src/system/push-server-origin.test.ts`, `packages/services/service-messaging/src/device-registry.ts`, `packages/services/service-messaging/src/objects/user-device.object.ts`, `packages/services/service-messaging/src/push-channel.ts` (`withOrigin`, unchanged on `main`), `packages/services/service-messaging/src/device-registry.integration.test.ts`, `packages/services/service-messaging/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-push/src/push-service.ts` (data forwarding), `packages/runtime/src/domains/notifications.ts` (as the PR cites it), `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` (the `text` column mapping), `.changeset/29768-push-device-origin-stored.md`

Inputs read: card #29768 body and all 6 comments (ruling B on #29642 as quoted in the body; the three should-fix items of 6595162668; claims 6670490478 / 6671550587; os-dev-report 6671567236); PR #30705 body, 19-file list, net diff vs `main` (merge-base `b77c160a`, 2 ahead / 13 behind); the docs-drift comment 6671569480; the 65 check-runs on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Retiring `[PLANNED — not yet stored]` is now TRUE.** On this head the chain is closed end to end: `registerOnce` builds one `values` object used by both the refresh `update` and the first `insert`, and it now carries `origin: request.origin ?? null`; `toUserDevice` sets `device.origin` when the row holds one and omits the member on `null`; `list()` is `listDevices`; `createPushChannel.send` calls `opts.devices.listDevices(recipient)` and passes `withOrigin(data, device.origin)` to `push.send`; `withOrigin` on `main` copies a value that `PushDeliveryDataSchema.shape.origin` accepts; both transports forward `data` whole (`push-service.ts`: FCM `message.data`, APNs top level). The runtime route already hands `RegisterDeviceRequestSchema.safeParse(body).data` to `registerDevice`, so `origin` reaches the registry. The new integration describe pins the chain with the real `ObjectQL`/`SqlDriver` registry and the real channel, and the flipped spec pin asserts no `PLANNED` on all three members. Declaration now equals enforcement; retiring the markers (and regenerating the two mdx rows) is correct.
- **Accept-set unchanged.** `PUSH_SERVER_ORIGIN_PATTERN`, `PUSH_SERVER_ORIGIN_MESSAGE`, optionality and the three schemas' structure are identical to `main`; only `.describe()` text and the docblock move, so the published JSON Schema `pattern` is the same (pinned by "publishes the same pattern in each JSON Schema"). No new export: `push-server-origin.ts` stays barrel-less. `Clause-②: no` is right.
- **Docblock statements checked against the regex** `^https?:\/\/(?:L(?:\.L)*|\[[0-9a-f:.]+\])(?::[0-9]{1,5})?$` with `L = [a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?`: (a) underscore refused — `_` is in no character class, so `http://my_svc:3000` fails; TRUE. (b) trailing dot refused — each `\.` must be followed by a label, so `https://crm.example.com.` cannot reach `$`; TRUE. (c) a dotted IPv4 host is admitted by the DNS arm — all-digit labels satisfy `L`; TRUE (the test already round-trips `http://192.168.1.20:3000`). (d) port is one to five digits, so `:443`, `:80`, a leading zero and 65536–99999 are admitted and nothing range-checks; TRUE (six digits are refused, which the docblock does not claim otherwise). (e) the bracketed arm admits any run of hex digits, colons and dots, `[:::]` included; TRUE, and lowercase hex only, consistent with the "lowercase host" sentence and with browser serialisation. (f) "a registration naming one is refused as a whole" — a Zod object parse fails on the member, so the route answers 400; TRUE. No statement in the docblock is false against the pattern.
- **Column.** `Field.text` with no `maxLength` and no index keying it maps to `TEXT` on every SQL dialect (`types.mdx`, text family), so the "unbounded" reasoning holds and the column cannot refuse a value the pattern accepts (a 253-character DNS name plus scheme and port exceeds 255). Existing deployments get the column through the additive sync (`ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN`). `UserDevice` is exported from the package index, so the object definition's `fields` gains a key; the spec's `UserDeviceSchema` already declared `origin`, so the published contract is unchanged and the implementation catches up to it.
- **Refresh semantics.** A refresh without `origin` stores `null` and clears the old value, the same overwrite `app_id` and `locale` already have; the `RegisterDeviceRequestSchema` docblock now names `origin` in the refresh list. Consistent and pinned.

### ② Semver level

Changeset: `@objectstack/service-messaging: patch`, `@objectstack/spec: patch`, body carrying `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, matching the PR body. Right by AGENTS.md's rule: the level follows the metadata-protocol kind alone, `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`; the `feat` prefix does not raise it. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: `sys_user_device` is an engine-owned system object, not a key a metadata author writes, so no authorable-surface ledger moves (`check:authorable-surface` reads the spec's metadata schemas via `gen:schema`, which this diff does not touch; `Spec property liveness` is green). The ledgers that do move are the object's eight translation bundles, regenerated and committed. The spec `patch` is owed because `.describe()` text ships in the published JSON Schema and docs.

Check-runs on `48036dd1`: 65 runs read, every one `completed` with `success` or `skipped` at read time, none in progress; `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Build Docs`, `Test Core (1–8/8)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` all `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none. The dev's out-of-scope note (the `PushMessage` docblock in `service-push` lists `notificationId` and `route` only) is taken up below as a should-fix.
- The three should-fix items of 6595162668 are answered by the docblock route, which that record allowed ("or name the limit in the docblock" / "or note that the Console is the one producer" / "should say an IPv4 host is accepted too"); the validator is untouched, as the card's claim required.
- Docs drift (6671569480): `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/push-service.mdx` lists `origin` among the registration members and says nothing about it being unstored, so it stays true; the release page is read-only and untouched.
- Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no out-of-relay login. The PR is a draft.
- Independence: rendered by an isolated contract-review subagent fed the card, the PR, the diff, the cited code on `main` and the check-runs, not the seat's conclusions; adopted by the seat named in `Reviewed-by:`.

### ④ Design judgment

- `protocol.zod.ts` — the description now states what the server does, and the refresh list names `origin`; holds against `registerOnce`.
- `push-device.zod.ts` — "Absent on a device registered without one" holds against `toUserDevice` (member omitted on `null`) and is pinned.
- `push-server-origin.ts` — the producer-bounded design is coherent: the shell compares the carried origin byte for byte with a saved server's, so an admitted non-canonical value can only fail to match, never name the wrong server; the narrower DNS-label arm costs a push its origin for `_` or trailing-dot hosts, and the docblock says so and tells the producer to omit the member. Against the ruling (store at registration, copy into every push) and the first consumer (`withOrigin`, then the mobile shell), the change holds.

Findings (none must-fix):

- **should-fix** — `packages/services/service-push/src/push-service.ts` `PushMessage` docblock describes the data as the notification id and `route` only; `origin` now rides there on every push to a device that registered one. A one-line addition, or a follow-up card beside #29042 so the Console producer and the transport docblock move together.
- **should-fix** — `RegisterDeviceRequestSchema` docblock: "refreshes that device (its token, vendor, app, locale and origin)". The refresh `values` also replace `platform` and `name`; the omission predates this PR but the hunk rewrote the sentence, so finish it.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-9eb7x4`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4cytQjG9X1CrCgytUM5`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7e4b969d9d223c01773a445e702dda9740a8ee0d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` + `packages/services/service-push/src/push-service.ts`, `.changeset/29768-push-device-origin-stored.md`, `packages/services/service-messaging/src/device-registry.ts` (the refresh `values` on `main`), `packages/spec/scripts/build-docs.ts` (what `gen:docs` projects), `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` (on this head)

Delta review of record 6672159811 (PASS on `48036dd1`): one commit, `7e4b969d` "docs(push,spec): name origin in the PushMessage data docblock and finish the refresh list", 3 files, +11/-6, folding in that record's two should-fix items. The rest of the tree is unchanged from the reviewed head and keeps that record's judgments; nothing below re-opens them.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set / public surface: unchanged.** The delta is two docblocks and one changeset line. No `.describe()`, pattern, member, export or route moves; `RegisterDeviceRequestSchema` and `PushMessage` parse and type exactly as before. `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` stand.
- **Refresh list is now complete and true.** The docblock names "token, vendor, platform, app, locale, origin and name"; the one `values` object `registerOnce` writes on both the refresh `update` and the first `insert` carries exactly those request members (`token`, `vendor`, `platform`, `app_id`, `locale`, `origin`, `name`) plus the server's own state (`enabled`, `invalidated_at`, `last_seen_at`), which are not request members and belong in no refresh list. Should-fix 2 of 6672159811 is closed.
- **`PushMessage` docblock is now true.** It names `origin` as a third data member, conditional on the device having registered one, and keeps the FCM `message.data` / APNs top-level placement sentence, which `withOrigin` and the transports' whole-`data` forwarding make accurate. Should-fix 1 of 6672159811 is closed.
- **No generated artifact is owed by the delta.** `build-docs.ts` projects the module doc block and the schemas' `.describe()` text; the per-schema TSDoc that moved is not projected (the "refreshes that device" row in `protocol.mdx` on this head is the `deviceId` member's own description, unchanged). So the two reference pages stay current without a regeneration, and `check:docs` has nothing to flag from this commit.

### ② Semver level

Changeset adds `'@objectstack/service-push': patch` with a bullet saying docblock only. Right: `@objectstack/service-push` is a released package (`18.2.0`, not private), the TSDoc ships in its `.d.ts`, and a `Metadata-protocol: none` change takes `patch`. The two existing `patch` lines and both declaration lines are unchanged. `Check Changeset` on `7e4b969d`: `completed · success`.

Check-runs on `7e4b969d` at read time (2026-11-05T23:28Z): 42 runs; `completed · success`: `filter`, `Spec property liveness`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Check PR Size`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Check Changeset`, `Auto Label`; `completed · skipped`: the usual opt-in and UI-artifact rows; **`in_progress`**: Type Check (4 jobs), Test Core (8/8 shards), Lint (7 jobs), Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI. None red when read. The delta is comment text and a changeset line, and the same families were green on `48036dd1`; the landing pre-check still reads them green on this head before queueing, as it must.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flags / `open_questions`: none new; the commit is the dev card thread's own (`session_016WV4czbHcjvoBYWDw2gRAq`).
- Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no out-of-relay login. The PR is still a draft.
- Independence: rendered by the same isolated contract-review subagent that rendered 6672159811, fed only the delta diff, the new head's check-runs and the cited code; adopted by the seat named in `Reviewed-by:`.

### ④ Design judgment

Both `hits` files hold against the code they describe: the refresh list against `registerOnce.values`, the data docblock against `withOrigin` and the transports. No design moved.

Findings (none must-fix):

- **should-fix (prose only)** — the PR body is now stale in two places: "Out of the file surface, left as is: the `PushMessage` docblock … does not name `origin`" and "The `RegisterDeviceRequestSchema` docblock's refresh list now names `origin` too" describe the `48036dd1` tree. Update both lines to the `7e4b969d` tree (the `service-push` docblock is in the diff, the refresh list is complete) so the body matches what lands.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-9eb7x4`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4cytQjG9X1CrCgytUM5`

**VERDICT: PASS**

Diff read at this head.
2. **Premise, measured:** contract review 6672159811 (PASS, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, head `48036dd1`) traced registration → row → channel → both transports; delta review 6672299353 (PASS, head `7e4b969d`) covers the docblock-only commit.
